laws.rule: For Pench Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra, the park requires an authorised guide in each safari vehicle, and visitors must show their park entry pass or identity proof when a forest official asks.
laws.heading: Pench Tiger Reserve FAQ: visitor rules

laws.rule: In Maharashtra Pench Tiger Reserve, passengers must not get out of a safari vehicle except at authorised places, lean out of it or move between vehicles.
laws.heading: Pench Tiger Reserve FAQ: visitor rules

laws.rule: Maharashtra Pench Tiger Reserve requires visitors to keep at least 20 metres from wildlife, avoid shouting at sightings, and not throw objects from their vehicle.
laws.heading: Pench Tiger Reserve FAQ: visitor rules

laws.rule: Maharashtra Pench Tiger Reserve sets a maximum speed of 20 km/h and requires at least 50 metres between vehicles. Vehicles must not overtake and must follow one-way rules where applicable.
laws.heading: Pench Tiger Reserve FAQ: visitor rules

laws.rule: Maharashtra Pench Tiger Reserve prohibits playing musical instruments or songs on phones or other devices during safari, and asks visitors to switch off mobile phones in the core.
laws.heading: Pench Tiger Reserve FAQ: visitor rules

laws.rule: At Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, visitors may not carry or consume alcoholic drinks and must not be under the influence of alcohol in the ecotourism zones.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve requires visitors not to be under the influence of narcotic or psychotropic substances in its ecotourism zones.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: Smoking is prohibited inside Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: At Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, visitors may get out of vehicles only at designated places; driving on closed trails, outside tourism areas or beyond designated hours is prohibited.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve prohibits lighting fires and admits visitors only in specially designated vehicles registered with the reserve authorities.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: At Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, pets are not allowed; visitors must not tease, chase, approach too closely or feed wild animals.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve prohibits plastic products inside the park and asks visitors to carry all litter outside; littering is a fineable offence.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve prohibits horns, shouting and music during a visit; it also prohibits mobile phones or similar gadgets that disturb the reserve.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: At Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, safari vehicles must not exceed 20 km/h and must maintain 50 metres between vehicles. The reserve requires a 20-metre distance from wild animals.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: For entry to Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, foreign visitors must show their original passport and valid entry ticket. The reserve says to carry original identification on safari and show it to forest officials when asked.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: For full-day photography in Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve’s core zone, the reserve says to apply to the field director with a valid online morning or evening safari booking for that date; special vehicle and gate limits apply.
laws.heading: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve safari rules

laws.rule: The Maharashtra Prohibition Act 1949 requires a licence or permit to buy, possess, use or drink liquor. Section 46 lets an authorised officer grant a visitor's permit for foreign liquor to a person visiting the State for no more than a week; it is ordinarily for up to a week at a time and extendable weekly to a total of one month.
laws.penalty_signal: Consuming or using an intoxicant against the Act (section 66(1)(b)): first offence up to 6 months and a fine of up to INR 10,000 (about A$149). Possessing, selling or transporting an intoxicant against the Act (section 65): 3 to 5 years and a fine of INR 25,000 to 50,000 (about A$373 to A$746), or both.

laws.rule: Under the Maharashtra Animal Preservation Act 1976 (as amended in 2015), no one may slaughter a cow, bull or bullock (section 5), transport one out of the State for slaughter (5A), buy or sell one for slaughter (5B), or possess its flesh if it was slaughtered against the Act (5C) or slaughtered outside Maharashtra (5D). A cow includes a heifer or a male or female calf. The accused carries the burden of proving the meat was lawful (section 9B).
laws.penalty_signal: Sections 5, 5A and 5B: up to 5 years or a fine of up to INR 10,000 (about A$149), or both. Possession of flesh, sections 5C and 5D: up to 1 year or a fine of up to INR 2,000 (about A$30). Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.
